newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL interbank rates fall, trading remains choppy.
newsitem.headline: KL interbank rates fall, trading remains choppy.

text.p: Interbank rates were lower compared with Friday's levels and dealers said more downside was likely after the sharp run-up last week.
"Rates are down but trading remains choppy. There's still some spillover effect," said a dealer at a Malaysian bank. "I think rates will be back to earlier levels soon."
Bank Negara said in a statement on Friday that the rise in money market rates was a temporary phenomenon.
It also said that its monetary policy stance remains unchanged.
One-, two- and three-week money were at 8.0/9.5 percent against 10.0/20.0 percent on Friday.
One- to six-month money fell to 7.5/8.0 percent from 8.5/9.0 percent.

The rise in interbank rates started on Thursday after Bank Negara intervened aggressively in the foreign exchange market to stem the slide of the ringgit. The central bank was said to have sold around $1 billion.
The intervention drained liquidity from the system, causing the market to be short and interbank rates to rise to unusually high levels.
The overnight rate, which was pushed up to as high as 25 percent on Friday, is expected to fall back to 8.0/10.0 percent, dealers said.
Interest rate futures on the Malaysia Monetary Exchange were generally higher.
At 0400 GMT, the benchmark three-month Kuala Lumpur Interbank Offered Rate (KLIBOR) June contract was up six points to 92.56, or an implied yield of 7.44 percent.
December rose seven to 92.58, or 7.42 percent, and March 1998 was up 10 to 92.55, or 7.45 percent.
